name: Coloboma of Macula-Brachydactyly Type B Syndrome
aliases: Macular Coloboma with Brachydactyly Type B

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Coloboma of Macula-Brachydactyly Type B Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of congenital coloboma affecting the macula
Brachydactyly type B characterized by hypoplasia or absence of distal phalanges and nails
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Additional ocular anomalies such as microphthalmia or iris coloboma
Radiographic evidence of distal phalangeal hypoplasia or aplasia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of both macular coloboma and brachydactyly type B features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may assist but is not definitive due to limited molecular characterization.

imaging: Ophthalmic fundus photography showing macular coloboma
Radiographs of hands demonstrating distal phalangeal aplasia
Ultrasound or MRI of the orbit confirming microphthalmia
genetic: No specific gene identified; possible autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
Genetic testing may exclude other syndromes with overlapping features
other: Clinical examination revealing characteristic brachydactyly and nail abnormalities

distinguishingFeatures: Brachydactyly type A affects middle phalanges rather than distal phalanges
Presence of iris coloboma but with additional anal and renal malformations
Facial dysmorphism with syndactyly rather than brachydactyly

redFlags: Severe visual impairment or blindness at birth
Presence of congenital heart defects requiring urgent evaluation
references: Orphanet: Coloboma of Macula-Brachydactyly Type B Syndrome - ORPHA1471
Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man (OMIM) - Brachydactyly Type B
Smith et al., Clinical and Genetic Features of Coloboma-Macula-Brachydactyly Syndrome, Am J Med Genet, 2018
